description: Category 1 (numerical) questions with integer answers, authored from the challenge sample questions and reference images in questions/office_1/questions.pdf. Objects are restricted to salient, visually verifiable furniture and decor so a human can confirm every answer from the scene. Each question carries a machine-readable spec that scripts/eval/verify_benchmark2.py re-evaluates against the iref_vla object bounding boxes.
notes: Q01 is the official Category 1 sample question from questions/office_1/questions.pdf; its answer (6) is the answer printed in the PDF.
difficulty: easy = single salient object class; medium = one relation; hard = two chained relations.
office_1 is a single open-plan room (one iref region), so no question needs a region restriction.

The scene has exactly two tables and questions never name them directly: the workstation table is identified by the six monitors on it and the conference table by the laptop on it, matching the phrasing style of the sample questions.

Folders and files are not used as count targets: iref annotates a whole row of binders on the bookcases as a single 'folder' object, so a human counting individual binders would not reproduce the number.
object_ids lists supporting iref_vla scene-graph ids for auditing; SAM3 should use target_objects.

questions.question: How many computer monitors are on the table closest to the map wall decal?
questions.evidence: All six monitors (2, 12, 18, 27, 36, 42) stand on the long workstation table 53, the table nearer the map wall decal on the east wall; the other table is the conference table across the room.

questions.question: How many chairs are in the office in total?
questions.evidence: Twelve office chairs: six at the workstation table (7, 26, 29, 58, 83, 85) and six around the conference table (21, 40, 45, 49, 52, 68).

questions.question: How many chairs are around the table with the laptop on it?
questions.evidence: Laptop 70 sits on conference table 50, which is ringed by six chairs (21, 40, 45, 49, 52, 68); the other six chairs belong to the workstation table.

questions.question: How many keyboards are on the table with the computer monitors?
questions.evidence: Six keyboards (3, 13, 19, 28, 37, 43) lie on workstation table 53, one per monitor, three facing each side.

questions.question: How many doors are in the office?
questions.evidence: Three brown wooden doors: 8 in the window wall, 38 in the east wall and 60 in the north wall behind the file cabinet.

questions.question: How many benches are in front of the windows?
questions.evidence: Two black benches (99, 107) line the glazed south wall under window 6.

questions.question: How many paper cups are on the file cabinet?
questions.evidence: Two paper cups stand on file cabinet 69: cup 79 in the coffee machine and cup 97 beside it; the third paper cup in the office is on the conference table.

questions.question: How many small potted cacti are on the table with the computer monitors?
questions.evidence: Three small potted cacti sit on workstation table 53: the pair 90 and 91 at the east end and 92 further along the same table.

questions.question: How many markers are on the table with the laptop on it?
questions.evidence: Three markers (74, 75, 76) lie next to laptop 70 on conference table 50; the remaining two markers in the office are on the workstation table.

questions.question: How many phones are on the table with the laptop on it?
questions.evidence: Phones 30 and 48 lie on conference table 50 alongside laptop 70; the third phone is the desk phone on the file cabinet.
